ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The asymptotic approximation of the log-magnitude versus frequency plot of a minimum phase system with real poles and one zero is shown in the figure. Its transfer function is ______.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows logarithmic magnitude-frequency asymptotes, with the vertical axis as dB and the horizontal axis as rad/s. The frequencies 0.1, 2, 5, and 25 rad/s are marked; at 0.1 rad/s the magnitude is marked as about 54 dB. The asymptote slopes in sequence are: from low frequency to before 2 rad/s is -40 dB/dec, from 2 to 5 rad/s is -60 dB/dec, from 5 to 25 rad/s is -40 dB/dec, and after 25 rad/s is -60 dB/dec. Then reason: The initial slope -40 dB/dec indicates that there are two poles at the origin, that is, the denominator contains s^2. At 2 rad/s the slope decreases again by 20 dB/dec, indicating there is one real pole s=-2. At 5 rad/s the slope increases by 20 dB/dec, indicating there is one real zero s=-5. At 25 rad/s the slope decreases by 20 dB/dec, indicating there is one real pole s=-25. Therefore the transfer function form is G(s)=K(s+5)/(s^2(s+2)(s+25)). Find K from the 54 dB at 0.1 rad/s in the figure: below all finite corner frequencies, |G(jω)|≈K·5/(ω^2·2·25)=K/(10ω^2). Taking ω=0.1, |G(j0.1)|≈10K. 54 dB corresponds to a magnitude of 10^(54/20)≈500, therefore 10K≈500, giving K≈50. So the transfer function is 50(s+5)/(s^2(s+2)(s+25)).
